     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RigidPushforwardRank
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.TwoTermEulerIndex
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# Scheme fibres and two-term Euler indices
    12	
    13	This file joins the scheme-theoretic fibre Euler index to the affine two-term
    14	finite-replacement machinery.  For a quasicoherent module on a family with a
    15	two-affine cover, the intrinsic index of a fibre is the signed kernel/cokernel
    16	index of the family Cech differential after residue-field base change.
    17	
    18	There are two scalar changes in the comparison.  First, the fibre index is
    19	defined over the scheme residue field `kappa(t)`, while the chart comparison
    20	uses `Gamma(Spec kappa(t), top)`.  Second, for a base `Spec R`, the family Cech
    21	differential is linear over `Gamma(Spec R, top)`, so its algebraic fibre is at
    22	the point transported from `t` along `Gamma(Spec R, top) equiv R`.
    23	
    24	The final theorem consumes an actual `TwoTermFiniteReplacement`.  Thus its
    25	right-hand side is the virtual rank of a finite projective module rather than
    26	an unpriced totalized finrank.  The left-hand side remains named an *index*:
    27	identifying it with geometric degree still requires cohomological finiteness,
    28	finite-pushforward Euler transfer, and Riemann--Roch.  Nothing here constructs
    29	a PicEt degree function or a representability consumer.
    30	
    31	## Main declarations
    32	
    33	* `AffineCoverMVSquare.chi_eq_moduleSectionDiffBase`: scalar-normalized Cech
    34	  index over global sections of the coefficient field.
    35	* `Hom.fiberEulerIndex_eq_baseChangedCechIndex`: comparison with the
    36	  residue-field base change of the family Cech differential.
    37	* `Hom.fiberEulerIndex_eq_baseChangedCechIndex_spec`: the same comparison at
    38	  the corresponding point of `Spec Gamma(Spec R, top)`.
    39	* `Hom.fiberEulerIndex_eq_virtualRank`: the finite-replacement virtual-rank
    40	  formula for the scheme-theoretic fibre index.
    41	-/
    42	
    43	set_option autoImplicit false
    44	
    45	universe u
    46	
    47	open CategoryTheory Limits Module TensorProduct
    48	
    49	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    50	
    51	noncomputable section
    52	
    53	namespace Scheme
    54	
    55	variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    56	
    57	/-- The concrete Cech index over a field agrees with the signed finranks of
    58	the base-linear section differential over `Gamma(Spec k, top)`.
    59	
    60	The underlying kernel and quotient modules are definitionally the same; only
    61	their scalar actions are transported along `Scheme.GammaSpecIso`.  No
    62	finite-dimensionality is asserted. -/
    63	theorem AffineCoverMVSquare.chi_eq_moduleSectionDiffBase
    64	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    65	    (V : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : C.left.Modules) :
    66	    letI := C.hom.baseSectionsModule M V.U₁
    67	    letI := C.hom.baseSectionsModule M V.U₂
    68	    letI := C.hom.baseSectionsModule M (V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂)
    69	    V.chi C M =
    70	      (Module.finrank Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)
    71	        (LinearMap.ker (V.moduleSectionDiffBase C.hom M)) : ℤ) -
    72	      (Module.finrank Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)
    73	        (Γ(M, V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂) ⧸
    74	          LinearMap.range (V.moduleSectionDiffBase C.hom M)) : ℤ) := by
    75	  letI m1 := C.hom.baseSectionsModule M V.U₁
    76	  letI m2 := C.hom.baseSectionsModule M V.U₂
    77	  letI m0 := C.hom.baseSectionsModule M (V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂)
    78	  have h0 : Module.finrank k (V.H0ₗ C M) =
    79	      Module.finrank Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)
    80	        (LinearMap.ker (V.moduleSectionDiffBase C.hom M)) := by
    81	    refine finrank_eq_of_ringEquiv_addEquiv
    82	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.symm
    83	      (AddEquiv.refl _) ?_
    84	    intro r x
    85	    rfl
    86	  have h1 : Module.finrank k (V.H1Cokₗ C M) =
    87	      Module.finrank Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)
    88	        (Γ(M, V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂) ⧸
    89	          LinearMap.range (V.moduleSectionDiffBase C.hom M)) := by
    90	    refine finrank_eq_of_ringEquiv_addEquiv
    91	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.symm
    92	      (AddEquiv.refl _) ?_
    93	    intro r x
    94	    rfl
    95	  rw [V.chi_def]
    96	  unfold AffineCoverMVSquare.h0 AffineCoverMVSquare.h1
    97	  rw [h0, h1]
    98	
    99	/-- The intrinsic fibre Euler index is the signed kernel/cokernel index of the
   100	family Cech differential after base change to
   101	`Gamma(Spec kappa(t), top)`.
   102	
   103	This combines the derived-to-Cech comparison on the fibre with the
   104	isomorphism of family and fibre Cech complexes.  It imposes no finiteness
   105	hypothesis, so its finranks retain their totalized meaning. -/
   106	theorem Hom.fiberEulerIndex_eq_baseChangedCechIndex
   107	    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffine Y] (V : X.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   108	    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] (t : Y)
   109	    [hfi : IsAffineHom (f.fiberι t)] :
   110	    letI : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤) :=
   111	      ((Y.fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom.toAlgebra
   112	    letI := f.baseSectionsModule M V.U₁
   113	    letI := f.baseSectionsModule M V.U₂
   114	    letI := f.baseSectionsModule M (V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂)
   115	    f.fiberEulerIndex t M =
   116	      (Module.finrank Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤)
   117	        (LinearMap.ker ((V.moduleSectionDiffBase f M).baseChange
   118	          Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤))) : ℤ) -
   119	      (Module.finrank Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤)
   120	        (TensorProduct Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤)
   121	          Γ(M, V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂) ⧸
   122	            LinearMap.range ((V.moduleSectionDiffBase f M).baseChange
   123	              Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤))) : ℤ) := by
   124	  letI aAB : Algebra Γ(Y, ⊤) Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤) :=
   125	    ((Y.fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom.toAlgebra
   126	  letI m1 := f.baseSectionsModule M V.U₁
   127	  letI m2 := f.baseSectionsModule M V.U₂
   128	  letI m0 := f.baseSectionsModule M (V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂)
   129	  let W := @AffineCoverMVSquare.preimage _ _ V (f.fiberι t) hfi
   130	  letI n1 := (f.fiberToSpecResidueField t).baseSectionsModule
   131	    (f.fiberModule t M) W.U₁
   132	  letI n2 := (f.fiberToSpecResidueField t).baseSectionsModule
   133	    (f.fiberModule t M) W.U₂
   134	  letI n0 := (f.fiberToSpecResidueField t).baseSectionsModule
   135	    (f.fiberModule t M) (W.U₁ ⊓ W.U₂)
   136	  rw [f.fiberEulerIndex_eq_cech t M W]
   137	  rw [W.chi_eq_moduleSectionDiffBase
   138	    (Over.mk (f.fiberToSpecResidueField t)) (f.fiberModule t M)]
   139	  change
   140	    (Module.finrank Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤)
   141	      (LinearMap.ker (W.moduleSectionDiffBase
   142	        (f.fiberToSpecResidueField t) (f.fiberModule t M))) : ℤ) -
   143	      (Module.finrank Γ(Spec (Y.residueField t), ⊤)
   144	        (Γ(f.fiberModule t M, W.U₁ ⊓ W.U₂) ⧸
   145	          LinearMap.range (W.moduleSectionDiffBase
   146	            (f.fiberToSpecResidueField t) (f.fiberModule t M))) : ℤ) =
   147	    _
   148	  rw [← finrank_ker_baseChange_residueField V f M t,
   149	    ← finrank_quotient_range_baseChange_residueField V f M t]
   150	
   151	/-- Over `Spec R`, the intrinsic fibre Euler index is the two-term family
   152	index at the corresponding point of `Spec Gamma(Spec R, top)`.
   153	
   154	Besides the geometric Cech comparison, this transports both the kernel and
   155	the quotient by the range across the residue-field algebra equivalence. -/
   156	theorem Hom.fiberEulerIndex_eq_baseChangedCechIndex_spec
   157	    {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec R)
   158	    (V : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent]
   159	    (t : Spec R) [IsAffineHom (p.fiberι t)] :
   160	    let B := Γ(Spec R, ⊤)
   161	    let ε : B ≃+* R :=
   162	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   163	    let H : PrimeSpectrum B ≃ₜ PrimeSpectrum R :=
   164	      PrimeSpectrum.homeomorphOfRingEquiv ε
   165	    let s := H.symm t
   166	    letI := p.baseSectionsModule M V.U₁
   167	    letI := p.baseSectionsModule M V.U₂
   168	    letI := p.baseSectionsModule M (V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂)
   169	    p.fiberEulerIndex t M =
   170	      (Module.finrank s.asIdeal.ResidueField
   171	        (LinearMap.ker ((V.moduleSectionDiffBase p M).baseChange
   172	          s.asIdeal.ResidueField)) : ℤ) -
   173	      (Module.finrank s.asIdeal.ResidueField
   174	        (TensorProduct B s.asIdeal.ResidueField Γ(M, V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂) ⧸
   175	          LinearMap.range ((V.moduleSectionDiffBase p M).baseChange
   176	            s.asIdeal.ResidueField)) : ℤ) := by
   177	  let B := Γ(Spec R, ⊤)
   178	  let ε : B ≃+* R :=
   179	    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   180	  let H : PrimeSpectrum B ≃ₜ PrimeSpectrum R :=
   181	    PrimeSpectrum.homeomorphOfRingEquiv ε
   182	  let s := H.symm t
   183	  let Kt := Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤)
   184	  letI : Field Kt :=
   185	    (MulEquiv.isField (Field.toIsField t.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   186	      (specResidueFieldRingEquiv R t).symm.toMulEquiv).toField
   187	  letI aBK : Algebra B Kt :=
   188	    (((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom.toAlgebra
   189	  letI m1 := p.baseSectionsModule M V.U₁
   190	  letI m2 := p.baseSectionsModule M V.U₂
   191	  letI m0 := p.baseSectionsModule M (V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂)
   192	  let hs : s.asIdeal = Ideal.comap ε.toRingHom t.asIdeal := rfl
   193	  let kappaMap := Ideal.ResidueField.map s.asIdeal t.asIdeal ε.toRingHom hs
   194	  have hkappaMap : Function.Bijective kappaMap :=
   195	    (RingEquiv.surjectiveOnStalks ε).residueFieldMap_bijective
   196	      s.asIdeal t.asIdeal hs
   197	  let kappaEquiv := RingEquiv.ofBijective kappaMap hkappaMap
   198	  let tau := kappaEquiv.trans (specResidueFieldRingEquiv R t)
   199	  let tauAlg : s.asIdeal.ResidueField ≃ₐ[B] Kt :=
   200	    AlgEquiv.ofRingEquiv fun b => by
   201	      change tau ((algebraMap B s.asIdeal.ResidueField) b) = _
   202	      change specResidueFieldRingEquiv R t
   203	        (kappaMap ((algebraMap B s.asIdeal.ResidueField) b)) = _
   204	      rw [Ideal.ResidueField.map_algebraMap]
   205	      exact (appLE_fromSpecResidueField_apply R t b).symm
   206	  let d := V.moduleSectionDiffBase p M
   207	  have hindex := p.fiberEulerIndex_eq_baseChangedCechIndex V M t
   208	  have h0 := finrank_ker_baseChange_of_algEquiv d tauAlg
   209	  have h1 := finrank_quotient_range_baseChange_of_algEquiv d tauAlg
   210	  exact hindex.trans (congrArg₂ (fun a b : ℕ => (a : ℤ) - (b : ℤ))
   211	    h0.symm h1.symm)
   212	
   213	/-- A finite replacement computes the intrinsic scheme-theoretic fibre Euler
   214	index as the virtual rank of its finite projective degree-zero term.
   215	
   216	The `TwoTermFiniteReplacement` hypothesis packages universal kernel and
   217	cokernel comparisons, so this result consumes both cohomological degrees.  It
   218	does not by itself identify the index with line-bundle degree. -/
   219	theorem Hom.fiberEulerIndex_eq_virtualRank
   220	    {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec R)
   221	    (V : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent]
   222	    (t : Spec R) [IsAffineHom (p.fiberι t)] :
   223	    letI := p.baseSectionsModule M V.U₁
   224	    letI := p.baseSectionsModule M V.U₂
   225	    letI := p.baseSectionsModule M (V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂)
   226	    ∀ F : AlgebraicJacobian.TwoTermFiniteReplacement
   227	        (V.moduleSectionDiffBase p M),
   228	    let B := Γ(Spec R, ⊤)
   229	    let ε : B ≃+* R :=
   230	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   231	    let H : PrimeSpectrum B ≃ₜ PrimeSpectrum R :=
   232	      PrimeSpectrum.homeomorphOfRingEquiv ε
   233	    let s := H.symm t
   234	    p.fiberEulerIndex t M =
   235	      (s.asIdeal.fiberRank F.K0 : ℤ) - (F.n : ℤ) := by
   236	  letI m1 := p.baseSectionsModule M V.U₁
   237	  letI m2 := p.baseSectionsModule M V.U₂
   238	  letI m0 := p.baseSectionsModule M (V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂)
   239	  intro F
   240	  rw [p.fiberEulerIndex_eq_baseChangedCechIndex_spec V M t]
   241	  exact F.fiberEulerIndex_eq_virtualRank _
   242

    11	/-!
    12	# The rank identity: the pushforward stalk rank is the fibre `h⁰`
    13	
    14	`AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.P1RankIdentity`
    15	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Sheaf.lean` §6) is the last open half of **leaf 3**
    16	of the `Scheme.HasRigidPushforward` gate factorization
    17	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardGate.lean`; `Picard/RigidPushforwardFrontier.lean`,
    18	item 2 of "what remains").  It says that for a finitely presented `M` on
    19	`ℙ¹_A` *whose two-term Čech complex already satisfies the conclusions of the
    20	algebraic engine* — `H⁰ = ker d` finite projective over `Γ(Spec A, ⊤)`, and the
    21	formation of `H⁰` commuting with arbitrary base change — the pointwise rank of
    22	the pushforward sections is the fibre invariant,
    23	`sectionsRankAtStalk (p_* M) t = p.fiberH0 M t`.
    24	
    25	This file proves it: `AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.p1RankIdentity_proved`.
    26	
    27	The `ℙ¹` consumer is a one-line specialisation of a general theorem,
    28	`AlgebraicGeometry.rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0`, whose statement mentions no
    29	projective line at all: it holds for any quasi-compact quasi-separated
    30	`p : X ⟶ Spec R` carrying a bundled two-chart affine cover
    31	`𝒰 : X.AffineCoverMVSquare`, and any quasi-coherent `M`.  That generality is
    32	deliberate, but it should not be oversold: the theorem is available to any
    33	family that *already carries* a two-affine Mayer–Vietoris cover of its total
    34	space, and the campaign's curve `C_A` is not known to be one — that is exactly
    35	why the curve side routes through `HasFiniteMapToP1` and
    36	`rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1Engine` instead
    37	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`).  What the generality does buy is that
    38	this leaf is independent of `ℙ¹`: it carries content whatever `ℙ¹_k` turns out
    39	to be, so it is not evidence about the `IsIntegral (ℙ¹_k)` leaf, and should not
    40	be read as such.
    41	
    42	## The route, in six steps
    43	
    44	Write `d := 𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase p M` for the base-linear two-term Čech
    45	differential, `κ(t)` for the residue field at `t : Spec R`, and `X_t`, `M_t`
    46	for the scheme-theoretic fibre and its induced module.
    47	
    48	1. **Sheaf condition on the base.**
    49	   `Scheme.Modules.pushforwardTopEquivBaseSections` followed by
    50	   `Scheme.AffineCoverMVSquare.globalSectionsEquivKerModuleSectionDiffBase`
    51	   gives `Γ(Spec R, p_* M) ≃ₗ[Γ(Spec R, ⊤)] ker d`.  So the engine's
    52	   finiteness and projectivity of `ker d` *are* finiteness and projectivity of
    53	   the pushforward sections.
    54	2. **`Module.rankAtStalk_eq`.**  For a finite projective — hence flat — module,
    55	   the stalk rank at `t` is `finrank κ(t) (κ(t) ⊗_R Γ(Spec R, p_* M))`.  This
    56	   is the only step that consumes `hfin` and `hproj`.
    57	3. **The engine's base-change conclusion at `B = κ(t)`.**  Bijectivity of
    58	   `AlgebraicJacobian.TwoTerm.kerBaseChange` at `B = Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤)` turns
    59	   `κ(t) ⊗ ker d` into `ker (d ⊗ κ(t))`.
    60	4. **The fibre-chart comparison.**  `exists_fiberChartTensorEquiv`
    61	   (`Picard/RigidPushforwardFiberChart.lean` §5) together with its restriction
    62	   naturality `fiberChart_smul_baseMap_res` (§6) identifies the whole
    63	   `κ(t)`-base-changed Čech square with the Čech square of the induced cover
    64	   `𝒰.preimage (p.fiberι t)` of `X_t`, hence `ker (d ⊗ κ(t))` with `ker d_t`
    65	   (`finrank_ker_baseChange_residueField` below).
    66	5. **Sheaf condition on the fibre.**  The same
    67	   `globalSectionsEquivKerModuleSectionDiffBase`, now for the fibre cover,
    68	   turns `ker d_t` into `Γ(X_t, M_t)`.
    69	6. **`fiberH0` by definition.**  `Scheme.Hom.fiberH0 p M t` *is*
    70	   `finrank κ(t) Γ(X_t, M_t)` for the `κ(t)`-structure
    71	   `Scheme.Hom.fiberSectionsModule`; only the scalars have to be transported
    72	   along `Scheme.ΓSpecIso (κ(t))`.
    73	
    74	Steps 2, 3 and 6 live over different but isomorphic scalar rings — `R` versus
    75	`Γ(Spec R, ⊤)`, and `κ(t)` versus `Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤)` — which is why the file
    76	opens with three transport bricks:
    77	
    78	* **Brick A** (`tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv`, `tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv_tmul`,
    79	  `finrank_tensor_eq_of_ringEquiv`, `finrank_ker_baseChange_of_algEquiv`,
    80	  `finrank_quotient_range_baseChange_of_algEquiv`): base-changed modules and
    81	  the two cohomology modules of a two-term complex have unchanged finrank
    82	  by a compatible pair of ring isomorphisms `σ : R ≃+* R'`, `τ : S ≃+* S'`
    83	  together with a `σ`-semilinear additive equivalence `e : N ≃+ N'`.  Pure
    84	  commutative algebra; `LinearEquiv.finrank_eq` cannot be used because the
    85	  scalar rings on the two sides are different objects, and no mathlib
    86	  counterpart was found.
    87	* **Brick B** (`specResidueFieldRingEquiv`,
    88	  `appLE_fromSpecResidueField_apply`): the residue field `κ(t)` of `Spec R`
    89	  versus `Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤)`, and the identification of the global-sections map
    90	  of `fromSpecResidueField t` with the residue map.  This was factored out of
    91	  a `have` currently buried inside
    92	  `exists_point_appLE_fromSpecResidueField_of_isMaximal`
    93	  (`Picard/RigidPushforwardFiberChart.lean` §9).
    94	* **Brick C** (`exists_fiberCechLinearEquiv`) is step 4.  §7 of
    95	  `Picard/RigidPushforwardFiberChart.lean` exports the commuting square as an
    96	  isomorphism of two-term complexes.  The kernel and quotient-by-range
    97	  consequences below consume that single comparison.
    98	
    99	## What the general theorem does — and does not — need
   100	
   101	Recorded honestly, because it changes what the consumers must supply:
   102	
   103	* `rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0` **does not use surjectivity of `d`**.  The
   104	  `hsurj` argument of `P1RankIdentity` is consequently unused in
   105	  `p1RankIdentity_proved`.  It is *not* implied by the other hypotheses —
   106	  do not delete it from a downstream statement on that reading.  (Take
   107	  `d = 0 : M₀ →ₗ M₁` with `M₁ ≠ 0` flat: then `ker d = M₀`, `d.baseChange B = 0`,
   108	  and `kerBaseChange d B` is the identity of `B ⊗ M₀`, bijective for every `B`,
   109	  while `d` is not surjective.)  The accurate claim is only that this proof
   110	  does not need it.  `hsurj` stays in the `Prop` because that `Prop` is pinned
   111	  by the gate, and its producer
   112	  (`p1Cech_h0_baseChange_of_fibrewise_h1_vanishing_of_p1TrivialConstants`)
   113	  hands out all four conclusions at once anyway.
   114	* It **does not need `[Algebra.FiniteType k A]`**, nor properness, nor finite
   115	  presentation of `M`.  The hypotheses actually used are `QuasiCompact p`,
   116	  `QuasiSeparated p`, quasi-coherence of `M`, and `IsAffineHom (p.fiberι t)`
   117	  (which is what makes the induced fibre cover a two-chart *affine* cover).
   118	
   119	## Why the projectivity hypothesis is load-bearing
   120	
   121	`hproj` is not decoration: dropped, the statement is **false**, and its
   122	consumers become vacuous.  Stated precisely, because the distinction has been
   123	got wrong here once already — the counterexample below witnesses the necessity
   124	of `hproj` **alone**.  In it `hsurj`, `hfin` and `hbc` all *hold*:
   125	`H¹(ℙ¹_k, 𝒪) = 0` so the Čech differential is surjective; `Γ = A/(x) = k` is
   126	cyclic hence finite over `A = k[x]`; and everything in the two-term complex is
   127	killed by `x`, so both `B ⊗ ker d` and `ker (d ⊗ B)` are `B/xB` and
   128	`kerBaseChange` is the canonical isomorphism for every `B`.  `hfin` and `hbc`
   129	are not separately witnessed here: they are what `Module.rankAtStalk_eq` and
   130	step 3 respectively *consume*.  The counterexample recorded at
   131	`Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Sheaf.lean`:567-576 is `A = k[x]` with
   132	`M = 𝒪_{ℙ¹_A}/x = coker(𝒪 --x--> 𝒪)`, which is finitely presented.  Then
   133	`Γ(ℙ¹_A, M) = A/(x) = k` is a *torsion* `A`-module, so `Module.rankAtStalk` at
   134	`t = (x)` takes its junk value `0`; but the fibre is `ℙ¹_k` with
   135	`M_t = 𝒪_{ℙ¹_k}`, so `p.fiberH0 M t = 1`.  What excludes it is exactly
   136	`Module.Projective` — `k` is not a projective `k[x]`-module — which is the
   137	hypothesis that licenses `Module.rankAtStalk_eq` in step 2.  `Module.Finite` is
   138	needed by the same lemma, and the `kerBaseChange` bijectivity is what makes
   139	step 3 an isomorphism rather than a one-way comparison map.
   140	
   141	`Module.finrank` returns the junk value `0` in the infinite-dimensional case,
   142	and it does so on *both* sides of the identity: `sectionsRankAtStalk` is a
   143	`Module.rankAtStalk`, and `fiberH0` is a `Module.finrank` over `κ(t)`.  So a
   144	priori the equality could hold vacuously as `0 = 0`.  Under the hypotheses it
   145	cannot: `ker d` is `Module.Finite` over `Γ(Spec R, ⊤)`, so `κ(t) ⊗ ker d` is a
   146	finite-dimensional `κ(t)`-vector space, and steps 3–6 are a chain of honest
   147	`κ(t)`-semilinear isomorphisms, whence `Γ(X_t, M_t)` is finite-dimensional too
   148	and both sides are genuine dimensions.
   149	
   150	Sources: Stacks 02KG (cohomology and base change, at `i = 0`), 00NX (finite
   151	projective = finite locally free), 01XJ; Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, II §5;
   152	EGA III 7.7, 7.9.9; Kleiman, *The Picard scheme* (FGA Explained), §5.
   153	-/

   165	/-! ## §1 (Brick A). Tensor transport across a pair of ring isomorphisms -/
   166	
   167	/-- **Semilinear transport of a tensor product along a pair of ring
   168	isomorphisms.**  Given ring isomorphisms `σ : R ≃+* R'` and `τ : S ≃+* S'`
   169	which intertwine the two algebra maps (`hστ`), and an additive equivalence
   170	`e : N ≃+ N'` which is `σ`-semilinear (`he`), this is the additive map
   171	`S ⊗[R] N →+ S' ⊗[R'] N'` determined by `s ⊗ₜ n ↦ τ s ⊗ₜ e n`.
   172	
   173	It is the comparison map exhibiting `S ⊗[R] N` and `S' ⊗[R'] N'` as the same
   174	module up to the change of scalars `τ`. -/
   175	noncomputable def tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv
   176	    {R R' : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing R']
   177	    {S S' : Type u} [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R' S']
   178	    {N N' : Type u} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [AddCommGroup N'] [Module R' N']
   179	    (σ : R ≃+* R') (τ : S ≃+* S')
   180	    (hστ : ∀ r : R, τ (algebraMap R S r) = algebraMap R' S' (σ r))
   181	    (e : N ≃+ N') (he : ∀ (r : R) (n : N), e (r • n) = σ r • e n) :
   182	    TensorProduct R S N →+ TensorProduct R' S' N' :=
   183	  TensorProduct.liftAddHom
   184	    (AddMonoidHom.mk'
   185	      (fun s => AddMonoidHom.mk' (fun n => τ s ⊗ₜ[R'] e n)
   186	        (fun n₁ n₂ => by simp [TensorProduct.tmul_add]))
   187	      (fun s₁ s₂ => by ext n; simp [TensorProduct.add_tmul]))
   188	    (fun r s n => by
   189	      change τ (r • s) ⊗ₜ[R'] e n = τ s ⊗ₜ[R'] e (r • n)
   190	      rw [he, Algebra.smul_def, map_mul, hστ, ← Algebra.smul_def, TensorProduct.smul_tmul])
   191	
   192	/-- **Value of the transport map on a pure tensor**: `tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv`
   193	sends `s ⊗ₜ n` to `τ s ⊗ₜ e n`. -/
   194	lemma tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv_tmul
   195	    {R R' : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing R']
   196	    {S S' : Type u} [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R' S']
   197	    {N N' : Type u} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [AddCommGroup N'] [Module R' N']
   198	    (σ : R ≃+* R') (τ : S ≃+* S')
   199	    (hστ : ∀ r : R, τ (algebraMap R S r) = algebraMap R' S' (σ r))
   200	    (e : N ≃+ N') (he : ∀ (r : R) (n : N), e (r • n) = σ r • e n) (s : S) (n : N) :
   201	    tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv σ τ hστ e he (s ⊗ₜ[R] n) = τ s ⊗ₜ[R'] e n :=
   202	  TensorProduct.liftAddHom_tmul _ _ s n
   203	
   204	/-- **The rank of a base-changed module is invariant under a compatible pair of
   205	ring isomorphisms.**  If `σ : R ≃+* R'` and `τ : S ≃+* S'` intertwine the two
   206	algebra maps and `e : N ≃+ N'` is `σ`-semilinear, then
   207	`Module.finrank S (S ⊗[R] N) = Module.finrank S' (S' ⊗[R'] N')`.
   208	
   209	This is the transport `LinearEquiv.finrank_eq` cannot provide, since it insists
   210	on a *fixed* scalar ring, whereas here the two sides are ranks over the
   211	literally different rings `κ(t)` and `Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤)` (respectively `R` and
   212	`Γ(Spec R, ⊤)` underneath).  No mathlib counterpart was found. -/
   213	theorem finrank_tensor_eq_of_ringEquiv
   214	    {R R' : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing R']
   215	    {S S' : Type u} [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R' S']
   216	    {N N' : Type u} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [AddCommGroup N'] [Module R' N']
   217	    (σ : R ≃+* R') (τ : S ≃+* S')
   218	    (hστ : ∀ r : R, τ (algebraMap R S r) = algebraMap R' S' (σ r))
   219	    (e : N ≃+ N') (he : ∀ (r : R) (n : N), e (r • n) = σ r • e n) :
   220	    Module.finrank S (TensorProduct R S N) = Module.finrank S' (TensorProduct R' S' N') := by
   221	  have hστ' : ∀ r' : R', τ.symm (algebraMap R' S' r') = algebraMap R S (σ.symm r') := by
   222	    intro r'; have := hστ (σ.symm r'); rw [σ.apply_symm_apply] at this
   223	    rw [← this, τ.symm_apply_apply]
   224	  have he' : ∀ (r' : R') (n' : N'), e.symm (r' • n') = σ.symm r' • e.symm n' := by
   225	    intro r' n'; apply e.injective
   226	    rw [e.apply_symm_apply, he, σ.apply_symm_apply, e.apply_symm_apply]
   227	  set f := tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv σ τ hστ e he with hf
   228	  set g := tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv σ.symm τ.symm hστ' e.symm he' with hg
   229	  have hgf : ∀ z : TensorProduct R S N, g (f z) = z := by
   230	    intro z
   231	    induction z using TensorProduct.induction_on with
   232	    | zero => simp
   233	    | add z₁ z₂ h₁ h₂ => rw [map_add, map_add, h₁, h₂]
   234	    | tmul s n => rw [hf, hg, tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv_tmul, tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv_tmul,
   235	        τ.symm_apply_apply, e.symm_apply_apply]
   236	  have hfg : ∀ z' : TensorProduct R' S' N', f (g z') = z' := by
   237	    intro z'
   238	    induction z' using TensorProduct.induction_on with
   239	    | zero => simp
   240	    | add z₁ z₂ h₁ h₂ => rw [map_add, map_add, h₁, h₂]
   241	    | tmul s' n' => rw [hf, hg, tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv_tmul, tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv_tmul,
   242	        τ.apply_symm_apply, e.apply_symm_apply]
   243	  have hsmul : ∀ (s : S) (z : TensorProduct R S N), f (s • z) = τ s • f z := by
   244	    intro s z
   245	    induction z using TensorProduct.induction_on with
   246	    | zero => simp
   247	    | add z₁ z₂ h₁ h₂ => rw [smul_add, map_add, map_add, h₁, h₂, smul_add]
   248	    | tmul s₀ n =>
   249	      rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', hf, tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv_tmul,
   250	        tensorAddHomOfRingEquiv_tmul, smul_eq_mul, map_mul, TensorProduct.smul_tmul',
   251	        smul_eq_mul]
   252	  exact finrank_eq_of_ringEquiv_addEquiv τ
   253	    (AddEquiv.ofBijective f ⟨Function.LeftInverse.injective hgf,
   254	      Function.RightInverse.surjective hfg⟩) hsmul
   255	
   256	/-- The dimension of the kernel of a base-changed linear map is unchanged when
   257	the coefficient-field algebra is replaced by an isomorphic one. -/
   258	theorem finrank_ker_baseChange_of_algEquiv
   259	    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
   260	    {M₀ M₁ : Type u} [AddCommGroup M₀] [Module R M₀]
   261	    [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁]
   262	    (d : M₀ →ₗ[R] M₁) {S T : Type u} [Field S] [Field T]
   263	    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R T] (e : S ≃ₐ[R] T) :
   264	    Module.finrank S (LinearMap.ker (d.baseChange S)) =
   265	      Module.finrank T (LinearMap.ker (d.baseChange T)) := by
   266	  let E₀ : (S ⊗[R] M₀) ≃ₗ[R] (T ⊗[R] M₀) :=
   267	    TensorProduct.congr e.toLinearEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl R M₀)
   268	  let E₁ : (S ⊗[R] M₁) ≃ₗ[R] (T ⊗[R] M₁) :=
   269	    TensorProduct.congr e.toLinearEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl R M₁)
   270	  have hsq : ∀ z : S ⊗[R] M₀,
   271	      E₁ (d.baseChange S z) = d.baseChange T (E₀ z) := by
   272	    intro z
   273	    induction z using TensorProduct.induction_on with
   274	    | zero => simp
   275	    | add z₁ z₂ h₁ h₂ => simp only [map_add, h₁, h₂]
   276	    | tmul s x => simp [E₀, E₁, LinearMap.baseChange_tmul]
   277	  let j : LinearMap.ker (d.baseChange S) ≃+ LinearMap.ker (d.baseChange T) :=
   278	    { toFun := fun x => ⟨E₀ x, by
   279	        rw [LinearMap.mem_ker, ← hsq, x.property, map_zero]⟩
   280	      invFun := fun y => ⟨E₀.symm y, by
   281	        rw [LinearMap.mem_ker]
   282	        apply E₁.injective
   283	        rw [map_zero, hsq, E₀.apply_symm_apply]
   284	        exact y.property⟩
   285	      left_inv := fun x => Subtype.ext (E₀.symm_apply_apply x)
   286	      right_inv := fun y => Subtype.ext (E₀.apply_symm_apply y)
   287	      map_add' := fun x y => Subtype.ext
   288	        (E₀.map_add (x : S ⊗[R] M₀) (y : S ⊗[R] M₀)) }
   289	  refine finrank_eq_of_ringEquiv_addEquiv e.toRingEquiv j ?_
   290	  intro s x
   291	  apply Subtype.ext
   292	  change E₀ (s • (x : S ⊗[R] M₀)) = e s • E₀ x
   293	  induction (x : S ⊗[R] M₀) using TensorProduct.induction_on with
   294	  | zero => simp

   298	/-- The dimension of the quotient by the range of a base-changed linear map is

   311	    Module.finrank S

   313	      Module.finrank T

   321	    TensorProduct.congr e.toLinearEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl R M₀)

   323	    TensorProduct.congr e.toLinearEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl R M₁)

   325	    { toFun := E₁
   326	      map_add' := E₁.map_add
   327	      map_smul' := by
   328	        intro s x
   329	        induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
   330	        | zero => simp
   331	        | add z₁ z₂ h₁ h₂ => simp only [smul_add, map_add, h₁, h₂]
   332	        | tmul s₀ m => simp [re, E₁, TensorProduct.smul_tmul', map_mul] }

   334	    { toFun := E₁.symm
   335	      map_add' := E₁.symm.map_add

   337	        intro t x
   338	        induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
   339	        | zero => simp
   340	        | add z₁ z₂ h₁ h₂ => simp only [smul_add, map_add, h₁, h₂]
   341	        | tmul t₀ m => simp [re, E₁, TensorProduct.smul_tmul', map_mul] }

   351	    rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
   352	    exact ⟨E₀ x, (hsq x).symm⟩

   355	    rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩

   362	    (LinearMap.range (d.baseChange S)) E₁inv hg

   365	    induction x using Submodule.Quotient.induction_on with
   366	    | _ x =>
   367	      rw [Submodule.mapQ_apply, Submodule.mapQ_apply]
   368	      exact congrArg Submodule.Quotient.mk (E₁.symm_apply_apply x)

   372	    | _ x =>

   374	      exact congrArg Submodule.Quotient.mk (E₁.apply_symm_apply x)

   376	      ((S ⊗[R] M₁) ⧸ LinearMap.range (d.baseChange S)) ≃ₛₗ[re.toRingHom]

    11	/-!
    12	# Serre finiteness for the section graded module (statement)
    13	
    14	The deep remaining input of the Hilbert-polynomial lane
    15	(`lem:sectionGradedModule_fg`, inbox `I-0109`): for a projective scheme over
    16	a field carrying a very ample line bundle `L` and a coherent sheaf `F`, the
    17	section graded ring `R(X, L) = ⊕ₘ Γ(X, L^{⊗m})` is Noetherian, the section
    18	graded module `M(X, F, L) = ⊕ₘ Γ(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗m})` is a finite module over it,
    19	and each graded component is a finite-dimensional `κ`-vector space.
    20	
    21	This file gives the **honest statement** against the projectivity vocabulary
    22	of `Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean` (the `IsProjectiveWith` closed-immersion
    23	predicate — very ampleness in the encoding settled in inbox `I-0118`), as a
    24	named typed `sorry` leaf: the proof is Serre's theorem ([Hartshorne] II.5.17
    25	ff., [Nitsure] §1) and is genuinely deep (multi-session; it needs the
    26	pushforward-to-projective-space reduction and cohomological finiteness on
    27	`ℙⁿ`).
    28	
    29	Compared with the blueprint node, which hypothesises an *ample* `L` and
    30	passes to a Veronese power, the Lean statement hypothesises the very ample
    31	form directly (`IsProjectiveWith`) — this is the form in which the
    32	Quot-scheme endgame ([Nitsure] §5) consumes it.
    33	
    34	Blueprint: `lem:sectionGradedModule_fg`
    35	(`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`).
    36	-/

    41	
    42	universe u
    43	
    44	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    45	
    46	/-- The structural `κ`-algebra structure on the global sections of a scheme
    47	over `Spec κ` (the absolute analogue of `Scheme.Hom.fiberResidueMap`). -/
    48	def Scheme.Hom.structuralSectionsHom {X : Scheme.{0}} {κ : Type} [CommRing κ]
    49	    (π : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) : κ →+* Γ(X, ⊤) :=
    50	  ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of κ)).inv ≫ π.appTop).hom
    51	
    52	/-- **Serre finiteness for the section graded module**
    53	(`lem:sectionGradedModule_fg`; [Nitsure] §1, [Hartshorne] II.5.17 ff.):
    54	for `π : X ⟶ Spec κ` projective carrying the very ample line bundle `L`
    55	and a coherent (finitely presented) sheaf `F` on `X`,
    56	
    57	1. the section graded ring `⊕ₘ Γ(X, L^{⊗m})` is Noetherian;
    58	2. the section graded module `⊕ₘ Γ(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗m})` is a finite module
    59	   over it;
    60	3. each component `Γ(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗m})` is a finite-dimensional `κ`-vector
    61	   space (via the structural `κ`-action).

    64	(inbox `I-0109`), awaiting the pushforward-to-`ℙⁿ` reduction and
    65	cohomological finiteness of coherent sheaves on projective space. -/

    67	    (π : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) (L F : X.Modules)

    81	/-! ## Descent to scheme-theoretic fibres — the Hilbert-lane connector
    82	
    83	The absolute leaf `sectionGradedModule_fg` is stated over a *field*; the Hilbert
    84	polynomial `Scheme.hilbertPolynomial` and its graded Hilbert function
    85	`Scheme.hilbertFunction` (`Picard/HilbertPolynomial.lean`) live at the
    86	scheme-theoretic fibre `X_s = π.fiber s` over the residue field `κ(s)`, which is
    87	a field.  The lemmas below are the sorry-free geometric glue that transports
    88	`IsProjectiveWith` and finite presentation to a fibre (both via the already
    89	proved `IsProjectiveWith.baseChange` and `Modules.pullback_isFinitePresentation`),
    90	so the deep Serre leaf applies fibrewise; the corollary
    91	`hilbertFunction_finiteDimensional` then shows the graded Hilbert function is a
    92	genuine (finite) dimension for projective fibres — the finiteness half of the
    93	bridge to `AlgebraicGeometry.gradedModule_hilbertSeries_rational`
    94	(inbox `I-0109`).  The remaining step — packaging finite generation as the
    95	`MvPolynomial`-finiteness input of that engine — is documented there. -/
    96	
    97	variable {X S : Scheme.{0}}
    98	
    99	/-- **`IsProjectiveWith` descends to scheme-theoretic fibres**: if `π : X ⟶ S`
   100	is projective carrying `L`, then the structural morphism of the fibre
   101	`X_s = π.fiber s`, namely `π.fiberToSpecResidueField s : X_s ⟶ Spec κ(s)`, is
   102	projective carrying the restriction `L_s = π.fiberModule s L`.  Immediate from
   103	`IsProjectiveWith.baseChange` along `S.fromSpecResidueField s`, since the fibre
   104	is the base change of `π` along that morphism (`Scheme.Hom.fiber`). -/
   105	theorem Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.fiber {π : X ⟶ S} {L : X.Modules}
   106	    (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) (s : S) :
   107	    (π.fiberToSpecResidueField s).IsProjectiveWith (π.fiberModule s L) :=
   108	  h.baseChange (S.fromSpecResidueField s)
   109	
   110	/-- **Finite presentation descends to scheme-theoretic fibres**: the restriction
   111	`F_s = π.fiberModule s F` of a finitely presented sheaf `F` to the fibre is
   112	finitely presented (pullback of a finitely presented sheaf along the fibre
   113	embedding `π.fiberι s`). -/

   119	/-- **Serre finiteness along a fibre** (`lem:sectionGradedModule_fg` specialised

   121	presented, the section graded ring of the fibre restriction `L_s` is Noetherian,
   122	and the section graded module of `F_s` is finite over it.  This is the deep leaf

   124	`IsProjectiveWith.fiber` and `fiberModule_isFinitePresentation`; it inherits the
   125	single named `sorry` of that leaf and no other.  The finite-dimensionality of
   126	each graded component — the third conclusion of `sectionGradedModule_fg`,
   127	matching the graded Hilbert function — is recorded separately as
   128	`hilbertFunction_finiteDimensional` (stated with the `Scheme.hilbertFunction`
   129	residue-field module structure). -/

   131	    (hproj : π.IsProjectiveWith L) (hF : F.IsFinitePresentation) :
   132	    (letI := Scheme.Modules.sectionGradedRing_gsemiring (π.fiberModule s L)

   135	       letI := Scheme.Modules.sectionGradedModule_gmodule
   136	         (π.fiberModule s F) (π.fiberModule s L)
   137	       Module.Finite (DirectSum ℕ (Scheme.Modules.sectionDeg (π.fiberModule s L)))

   142	      (Scheme.Hom.fiberModule_isFinitePresentation π s hF)).1,
   143	   (sectionGradedModule_fg (π.fiberToSpecResidueField s) (π.fiberModule s L)
   144	      (π.fiberModule s F) (hproj.fiber s)
   145	      (Scheme.Hom.fiberModule_isFinitePresentation π s hF)).2.1⟩
   146	
   147	/-- **The graded Hilbert function is a genuine (finite) dimension for projective
   148	fibres**: for `π : X ⟶ S` projective carrying `L` and `F` finitely presented,

   171	endomorphisms and finite over the polynomial ring `κ[X₀,…,X_{r-1}]` — into a
   172	rational Hilbert function (`AlgebraicGeometry.IsRatHilb`).  To feed the geometric

   183	
   184	/-- **Engine-ready packaging of Serre finiteness** for a Hilbert function
   185	`f : ℕ → ℕ` over a field `κ`: a finitely generated (over a polynomial ring in `r`
   186	degree-one variables) `ℕ`-graded `κ`-vector space whose `n`-th graded piece has
   187	dimension `f n`.  This bundles exactly the data and hypotheses consumed by the
   188	graded Hilbert–Serre rationality engine
   189	`AlgebraicGeometry.gradedModule_hilbertSeries_rational`; the engine call is
   190	`GradedHilbert.isRatHilb`.  Geometrically `M` is the fibre section module
   191	`⊕ₘ Γ(X_s, F_s ⊗ L_s^{⊗m})`, `grading n` is its `n`-th piece, and `gen` are the
   192	`d+1` multiplications by the homogeneous coordinate sections. -/
   193	structure GradedHilbert (κ : Type u) [Field κ] (f : ℕ → ℕ) where
   194	  /-- Number of degree-one polynomial generators (`d+1` homogeneous coordinates). -/
   195	  r : ℕ
   196	  /-- The ambient graded `κ`-vector space. -/
   197	  M : Type u
   198	  [addCommGroup : AddCommGroup M]
   199	  [module : Module κ M]
   200	  /-- The internal `ℕ`-grading. -/
   201	  grading : ℕ → Submodule κ M
   202	  [decomposition : DirectSum.Decomposition grading]
   203	  /-- Each graded piece is finite-dimensional. -/
   204	  finiteDimensional : ∀ n, FiniteDimensional κ (grading n)
   205	  /-- The `r` commuting degree-one endomorphisms (coordinate multiplications). -/
   206	  gen : Fin r → Module.End κ M
   207	  /-- The generators commute. -/
   208	  gen_comm : ∀ i j, Commute (gen i) (gen j)
   209	  /-- Each generator raises the grading degree by one. -/
   210	  gen_raisesDegree : ∀ i, GradedModule.RaisesDegree grading (gen i)
   211	  /-- The graded pieces realise the prescribed dimensions `f`. -/
   212	  finrank_grading : ∀ n, Module.finrank κ (grading n) = f n
   213	  /-- `M` is finite over the polynomial ring `κ[X₀,…,X_{r-1}]` acting via `gen`. -/
   214	  finite : letI := GradedModule.polyModule gen gen_comm
   215	    Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin r) κ) M

   226	dimension identification `GradedHilbert.finrank_grading`. -/
   227	theorem GradedHilbert.isRatHilb {κ : Type u} [Field κ] {f : ℕ → ℕ}
   228	    (H : GradedHilbert κ f) : IsRatHilb (fun n => (f n : ℚ)) H.r := by
   229	  -- The carried instances are found via the structure's projection instances
   230	  -- (registered above), matching the terms in `H.finite`'s type exactly, so the
   231	  -- finiteness argument unifies without a `polyModule`/`compHom` `whnf` blow-up.

   234	      H.gen_raisesDegree H.finite

   236	      = fun n => (Module.finrank κ (H.grading n) : ℚ) := by
   237	    funext n; rw [H.finrank_grading]
   238	  rw [hfun]; exact h

   549	/-- **A two-term finite replacement** of the complex `d : M0 → M1`
   550	(Mumford AV II §5 Lemma 1; EGA III 6.10.5): a two-term complex
   551	`k : K0 → A^n` with `K0` finite projective and `A^n` finite free, together
   552	with a quasi-isomorphism `(a0, a1) : K• → M•` whose formation commutes with
   553	arbitrary base change: for every commutative `A`-algebra `B` the induced
   554	maps `H⁰(K• ⊗ B) → H⁰(M• ⊗ B)` and `H¹(K• ⊗ B) → H¹(M• ⊗ B)` are bijective.
   555	
   556	Audit (see the file docstring): `K0` finite *free* is not achievable
   557	globally — only finite projective — and projectivity is what the consumers
   558	(local freeness of `H⁰`, minor/Fitting loci of `k`) actually use; after
   559	localization `K0` becomes free and `k` a matrix. -/
   560	structure TwoTermFiniteReplacement (d : M0 →ₗ[A] M1) : Type (u + 1) where
   561	  /-- The rank of the degree-1 finite free term `K¹ = A^n`. -/
   562	  n : ℕ
   563	  /-- The degree-0 term of the replacement complex. -/
   564	  K0 : Type u
   565	  [addCommGroup_K0 : AddCommGroup K0]
   566	  [module_K0 : Module A K0]
   567	  /-- The differential `K⁰ → K¹ = A^n` of the replacement complex. -/
   568	  k : K0 →ₗ[A] (Fin n → A)
   569	  /-- The degree-0 leg of the quasi-isomorphism `K• → M•`. -/
   570	  a0 : K0 →ₗ[A] M0
   571	  /-- The degree-1 leg of the quasi-isomorphism `K• → M•`. -/
   572	  a1 : (Fin n → A) →ₗ[A] M1
   573	  /-- `K⁰` is finitely generated. -/
   574	  finite_K0 : Module.Finite A K0
   575	  /-- `K⁰` is projective (finite free is impossible globally; see audit). -/
   576	  projective_K0 : Module.Projective A K0
   577	  /-- `(a0, a1)` is a map of complexes. -/
   578	  comm : d ∘ₗ a0 = a1 ∘ₗ k
   579	  /-- The `H⁰` comparison map is bijective after arbitrary base change. -/
   580	  h0_bijective : ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B],
   581	    Function.Bijective
   582	      (h0Map (k.baseChange B) (d.baseChange B) (a0.baseChange B) (a1.baseChange B)
   583	        (baseChange_square k d a0 a1 B comm))

   585	  h1_bijective : ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B],
   586	    Function.Bijective
   587	      (h1Map (k.baseChange B) (d.baseChange B) (a0.baseChange B) (a1.baseChange B)

   594	/-- **Existence of the two-term finite replacement** (Mumford AV II §5
   595	Lemma 1, two-term case).  If `A` is noetherian, `M0`, `M1` are flat, and
   596	`H⁰ = ker d`, `H¹ = coker d` are finitely generated, then `d` admits a
   597	two-term finite replacement in the sense of `TwoTermFiniteReplacement`. -/
   598	theorem exists_twoTermFiniteReplacement [IsNoetherianRing A]
   599	    [Module.Flat A M0] [Module.Flat A M1] (d : M0 →ₗ[A] M1)

   605	  choose y hy using fun i => Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective (range d) (s i)
   606	  set a1 : (Fin n → A) →ₗ[A] M1 := Fintype.linearCombination A y with ha1
   607	  have hsurj1 : Function.Surjective ((range d).mkQ ∘ₗ a1) := by
   608	    rw [← range_eq_top, range_comp, ha1, Fintype.range_linearCombination,
   609	      Submodule.map_span, ← Set.range_comp]
   610	    have hys : ((range d).mkQ ∘ y) = s := funext fun i => hy i
   611	    rw [hys, hs]
   612	  have hcover : ∀ z : M1, ∃ v : Fin n → A, z - a1 v ∈ range d := by
   613	    intro z
   614	    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hsurj1 (Submodule.Quotient.mk z)
   615	    refine ⟨v, ?_⟩
   616	    have hv' : Submodule.Quotient.mk (a1 v) = (Submodule.Quotient.mk z : M1 ⧸ range d) := hv
   617	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.eq] at hv'
   618	    rw [← neg_sub]
   619	    exact (range d).neg_mem hv'
   620	  -- Step 2: the surjection `g : M0 × A^n → M1` and its kernel, the fibre product.
   621	  set g : (M0 × (Fin n → A)) →ₗ[A] M1 :=
   622	    d ∘ₗ LinearMap.fst A M0 (Fin n → A) - a1 ∘ₗ LinearMap.snd A M0 (Fin n → A) with hgdef
   623	  have hgapply : ∀ p : M0 × (Fin n → A), g p = d p.1 - a1 p.2 := fun p => rfl
   624	  have hg : Function.Surjective g := by

   626	    obtain ⟨v, x, hx⟩ := hcover z
   627	    refine ⟨(x, -v), ?_⟩
   628	    rw [hgapply]
   629	    simp only [map_neg, sub_neg_eq_add]
   630	    rw [hx]

   632	  set N := ker g with hNdef
   633	  have hexact : Function.Exact N.subtype g := g.exact_subtype_ker_map
   634	  have hι : Function.Injective N.subtype := Submodule.injective_subtype N

   636	  set a0 : N →ₗ[A] M0 := LinearMap.fst A M0 (Fin n → A) ∘ₗ N.subtype with ha0
   637	  have hcomm : d ∘ₗ a0 = a1 ∘ₗ k := by
   638	    ext x
   639	    change d x.1.1 = a1 x.1.2

   643	      = Submodule.map (LinearMap.inl A M0 (Fin n → A)) (ker d) := by
   644	    ext p
   645	    simp only [Submodule.mem_inf, mem_ker, hNdef, Submodule.mem_map]
   646	    constructor
   647	    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩

   649	      have h1' : d p.1 - a1 p.2 = 0 := h1
   650	      rw [h2', map_zero, sub_zero] at h1'
   651	      exact ⟨p.1, h1', Prod.ext rfl h2'.symm⟩
   652	    · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
   653	      constructor
   654	      · change d x - a1 (0 : Fin n → A) = 0

   656	        exact hx
   657	      · rfl
   658	  have hNfg : N.FG := by
   659	    apply Submodule.fg_of_fg_map_of_fg_inf_ker (LinearMap.snd A M0 (Fin n → A))
   660	    · exact IsNoetherian.noetherian _
   661	    · rw [hker_inf]
   662	      exact hH0.map _

   694	          = d.baseChange B ((LinearMap.fst A M0 (Fin n → A)).baseChange B u)

   696	      intro u
   697	      have hg' : g.baseChange B
   698	          = d.baseChange B ∘ₗ (LinearMap.fst A M0 (Fin n → A)).baseChange B
   699	            - a1.baseChange B ∘ₗ (LinearMap.snd A M0 (Fin n → A)).baseChange B := by
   700	        rw [hgdef, baseChange_sub, baseChange_comp, baseChange_comp]
   701	      rw [hg']
   702	      rfl
   703	    have hkBC : k.baseChange B
   704	        = (LinearMap.snd A M0 (Fin n → A)).baseChange B ∘ₗ N.subtype.baseChange B := by
   705	      rw [hk, baseChange_comp]
   706	    have ha0BC : a0.baseChange B
   707	        = (LinearMap.fst A M0 (Fin n → A)).baseChange B ∘ₗ N.subtype.baseChange B := by
   708	      rw [ha0, baseChange_comp]
   709	    constructor
   710	    · rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
   711	      rintro ⟨z, hzmem⟩ hz
   712	      have hz0 : a0.baseChange B z = 0 := by

   714	      have hzk : k.baseChange B z = 0 := mem_ker.mp hzmem

   716	      rw [hkBC, LinearMap.comp_apply] at hzk

   726	          exact hzk
   727	        exact Prod.ext e1 e2

   729	        apply (TensorProduct.prodRight A B B M0 (Fin n → A)).injective
   730	        rw [hu, map_zero]

   732	        apply hpure B

   735	      exact Subtype.ext hz2

   790	/-- **The split-off corollary on a replacement** (the B5 gate input): if
   791	`H¹ = coker d` vanishes, i.e. `d` is surjective, then the differential `k`
   792	of any finite replacement is surjective onto the finite free `K¹ = A^n` —
   793	hence split by projectivity of `A^n`, so `K⁰ ≅ ker k ⊕ A^n` with `ker k`
   794	finite projective realizing `H⁰`.  Proved by descending the `H¹` comparison
   795	at `B = A` along `TensorProduct.lid`. -/
   796	theorem TwoTermFiniteReplacement.k_surjective_of_surjective
   797	    {d : M0 →ₗ[A] M1} (R : TwoTermFiniteReplacement d)

   799	  apply surjective_of_baseChange_self
   800	  rw [← range_eq_top, ← Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff]
   801	  haveI h1 : Subsingleton ((A ⊗[A] M1) ⧸ range (d.baseChange A)) := by
   802	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.subsingleton_iff, range_eq_top]
   803	    exact LinearMap.baseChange_surjective A hd
   804	  exact ⟨fun a b => (R.h1_bijective A).injective (Subsingleton.elim _ _)⟩

     8	/-!
     9	# The fibre `h⁰` comparison, without projectivity
    10	
    11	**The bridge B5 needs, and the one `rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0` cannot give.**
    12	
    13	`AlgebraicGeometry.rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0` (`Picard/RigidPushforwardRank.lean`)
    14	proves `sectionsRankAtStalk (p_* M) t = p.fiberH0 M t` under three hypotheses
    15	`hfin`, `hproj`, `hbc`.  Its own module docstring establishes that `hproj`
    16	(`Module.Projective` of the Čech `H⁰`) is **load-bearing**: dropped, the
    17	statement is false, with the counterexample `A = k[x]`,
    18	`M = 𝒪_{ℙ¹_A}/x` recorded at `Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Sheaf.lean`:567-576.
    19	
    20	That is true of *that* statement, and it has been read as a bound on what the
    21	machinery can deliver.  It is not.  Reading which step consumes which
    22	hypothesis shows `hfin` and `hproj` are used **only in step 1**, the appeal to
    23	`Module.rankAtStalk_eq` that converts `sectionsRankAtStalk` — a
    24	`Module.rankAtStalk`, which is a statement about the module being flat — into a
    25	fibre dimension.  Steps 2 through 6, the entire semilinear transport
    26	
    27	```
    28	κ(t)-fibre of Γ(p_* M, ⊤)  ≅  κ(t) ⊗ ker d  ≅  ker (d ⊗ κ(t))
    29	                           ≅  ker d_t       ≅  Γ(X_t, M_t)
    30	```
    31	
    32	consume **neither `hfin` nor `hproj`** — verified by a fresh-context review,
    33	which reproduced the original from this theorem by adding only
    34	`Module.rankAtStalk_eq`.  So this file states the comparison with those two
    35	hypotheses removed:
    36	
    37	* `fiberRank_gammaTop_eq_fiberH0` — no `hfin`, no `hproj`, only `hbc`.
    38	
    39	**But dropping `hfin` has a cost, and it must be stated here rather than
    40	discovered later.**  The original's docstring
    41	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardRank.lean`:138-145) closes a junk-value hazard:
    42	`Module.finrank` returns `0` in the infinite-dimensional case, on *both* sides,
    43	so the identity could hold vacuously as `0 = 0`.  Its argument that this cannot
    44	happen runs entirely through `hfin` (`ker d` finite ⟹ `κ(t) ⊗ ker d` is
    45	finite-dimensional ⟹ steps 3-6 carry that to `Γ(X_t, M_t)`).  `hbc` does **not**
    46	replace it: taking `d = 0 : M₀ →ₗ[A] PUnit` makes `hbc` hold for every `B`
    47	(trivially surjective) with `ker d = M₀` arbitrary, so an infinite-dimensional
    48	`ker d` is compatible with `hbc` and both sides then read `0`.
    49	
    50	So the theorem below is honest but weaker than the original in a way the
    51	hypothesis list alone does not show: **it is informative only where `ker d` is
    52	finite-dimensional over `κ(t)`**, and it does not certify that itself.  A
    53	consumer wanting a non-vacuous reading must supply finite-dimensionality
    54	separately — which is *not* the same as supplying `hfin` (`Module.Finite` over
    55	the base), and is the reason the statement is still worth having.
    56	
    57	## What this buys for B5, and the obligation it does NOT remove
    58	
    59	`Scheme.HasH0Semicontinuity` (`Picard/SemicontinuityH0.lean`) asks for openness
    60	of `{t | q.fiberH0 L t ≤ n}`.  The `sectionsRankAtStalk` form cannot be an input
    61	to it: semicontinuity is only informative where the fibre dimension *jumps*, and
    62	`hproj` forces it locally constant (`Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk`).
    63	The `Ideal.fiberRank` form here has no such effect, which is the point of the
    64	restatement.
    65	
    66	**It does not, however, already match
    67	`Scheme.Modules.isOpen_pointRank_le`** (`Picard/PointRankSemicontinuity.lean`),
    68	and an earlier revision of this docstring claimed it did.  Measured: the two are
    69	*not the same term* and `rfl` between them fails.  `pointRank` unfolds (through
    70	`pointRank_eq_chartFiberRank` at `V = ⊤`) to a `fiberRank` taken at a prime of
    71	`Γ(Spec R, ⊤)` with the `Γ(Spec R, ⊤)`-module structure, whereas the conclusion
    72	below uses `t.asIdeal` for `t : PrimeSpectrum R` with the `R`-module structure.
    73	Bridging them needs a `ΓSpecIso` transport of exactly the kind steps 2 and 6
    74	perform by hand, and the only in-tree lemma relating the two worlds,
    75	`Scheme.Modules.rankAtStalk_sections_eq_pointRank`
    76	(`Picard/FlatteningStratificationUniversal.lean`:204), carries
    77	`[Module.Flat]` + `[Module.Finite]` binders — i.e. precisely what was dropped.
    78	
    79	So B5 has **three** open obligations, not one: (a) `hbc` without
    80	`h¹`-vanishing, (b) finite-dimensionality to defeat the junk-value reading, and
    81	(c) this carrier bridge between `pointRank` and `Ideal.fiberRank`.  (c) was
    82	unlisted until a fresh-context review found it.
    83	
    84	**CORRECTED, and both corrections are against this list, not against the Lean
    85	below.** Two of those three have since been repriced or closed:
    86	
    87	* **(b) is CLOSED** — `Picard/TwoTermKernelSemicontinuity.lean`.  Stated on a
    88	  two-term complex `k : K → Aⁿ` with `K` merely `Module.Finite`,
    89	  finite-dimensionality of both fibres is *synthesised*, not supplied: it is a
    90	  consequence of the shape, so no hypothesis defeats the junk-value reading —
    91	  there is nothing to defeat.
    92	* **(a) was MISPRICED, and the misprice is mine.**  The counterexample below is
    93	  correct and `hbc` really is not free.  But `hbc` is consumed in **step 3
    94	  only**, whose job is to cross from `ker (d ⊗ κ(t))` to `κ(t) ⊗ ker d` — that
    95	  is, to reach *this* theorem's conclusion about `Γ(p_* M, ⊤)`.  Steps 4-6 alone
    96	  already give `dim ker (d ⊗ κ(t)) = p.fiberH0 M t`, with no `hbc` at all;
    97	  that is `finrank_ker_moduleSectionDiffBase_baseChange_eq_fiberH0`
    98	  (`Picard/FiberH0CechKernel.lean`).  So `hbc` identifies the fibre of the
    99	  *pushforward's section module*; it does **not** identify the fibre `h⁰`, and a
   100	  route through the fibrewise Čech kernel does not owe it.
   101	
   102	(c) stands, unchanged.  What replaces (a) is a different obligation: the Čech
   103	difference map must be *replaced* by a complex of the engine's shape, and
   104	`TwoTermFiniteReplacement.h0_bijective` — not `kerBaseChange` — is where the
   105	residual cohomology-and-base-change content sits.
   106	
   107	## What is still open
   108	
   109	The remaining hypothesis `hbc` — bijectivity of
   110	`AlgebraicJacobian.TwoTerm.kerBaseChange` over every algebra — is *not* free,
   111	and it is worth being precise about why, because the temptation is to hope it
   112	falls out of flatness.
   113	
   114	Its only producer in the tree,
   115	`TwoTerm.bijective_kerBaseChange_of_surjective`, needs `d` **surjective** —
   116	i.e. `h¹`-vanishing.  Surjectivity is genuinely necessary and not an artefact
   117	of that proof: take `A = ℤ`, `d = (2 · ·) : ℤ → ℤ`, which is injective with
   118	both terms flat but not surjective.  Then `ker d = 0`, so `B ⊗ ker d = 0` for
   119	every `B`, while over `B = ℤ/2` the base-changed map is zero and
   120	`ker (d ⊗ B) = ℤ/2 ≠ 0`.  So `kerBaseChange` is not bijective, with flatness
   121	of both terms intact.
   122	
   123	What this file therefore does is **relocate** part of the B5 obligation, not
   124	discharge it.  It converts "find a projectivity-free rank bridge" — impossible,
   125	and the route the gate's own docstring prescribes — into the three named items
   126	(a), (b), (c) above, of which (a) is the honest half of
   127	cohomology-and-base-change (Stacks 02KG).  Correctly located; all three open.
   128	
   129	One route not yet followed: a `TwoTermFiniteReplacement` supplies
   130	`h0_bijective` for *every* algebra `B` with **no** surjectivity hypothesis
   131	(it is a field of the structure, and `exists_twoTermFiniteReplacement` needs
   132	only noetherian + flat + f.g. cohomology).  That is a comparison between the
   133	`H⁰`s of the replacement and original complexes rather than the
   134	`kerBaseChange` of one map, so it does not immediately give `hbc`; whether it
   135	can be made to is the next thing to try.
   136	
   137	## References
   138	
   139	Stacks 02KG (cohomology and base change at `i = 0`), 00NX; Mumford,
   140	*Abelian Varieties*, II §5; Hartshorne III 12.8, 12.11.
   141	-/

     8	/-!
     9	# The fibre `h⁰` is the fibrewise Čech kernel — with no base-change hypothesis
    10	
    11	**A repricing, and it corrects obligation (a) of the three recorded at
    12	`Picard/FiberH0Comparison.lean`:79-82.**
    13	
    14	`fiberRank_gammaTop_eq_fiberH0` (same file) proves
    15	
    16	```
    17	dim_κ(t) (κ(t)-fibre of Γ(p_* M, ⊤))  =  p.fiberH0 M t
    18	```
    19	
    20	assuming `hbc`: bijectivity of `TwoTerm.kerBaseChange` over **every** algebra.
    21	That hypothesis was recorded as the honest half of cohomology-and-base-change,
    22	not free, with a counterexample showing it fails without surjectivity of the
    23	differential (`A = ℤ`, `d = ·2`, `B = ℤ/2`).  All of that is correct.
    24	
    25	What was **not** noticed: `hbc` is consumed in exactly one place, *step 3*, whose
    26	only job is to move from `κ(t) ⊗ ker d` to `ker (d ⊗ κ(t))` — i.e. to reach the
    27	pushforward's *own* section module.  Steps 4, 5 and 6 alone already prove
    28	
    29	```
    30	dim_κ(t) ker (d ⊗ κ(t))  =  p.fiberH0 M t
    31	```
    32	
    33	with **no `hbc`, no `hfin`, no `hproj`, and no `h¹`-vanishing** — where `d` is
    34	the Čech difference map `𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase p M`.  That is the statement
    35	below, and it is the one a semicontinuity argument wants: the *left* side is a
    36	kernel of a base-changed map, which is what an upper-semicontinuity engine can
    37	say something about, whereas `Γ(p_* M, ⊤)`'s fibre is not.
    38	
    39	So the pricing was right about `hbc` and wrong about who needs it.  `hbc` is
    40	needed to identify the fibre of the **pushforward's sections**; it is not needed
    41	to identify the fibre `h⁰`.  A lane routing semicontinuity through the fibrewise
    42	Čech kernel does not owe it at all.
    43	
    44	## What this composes with, and what remains
    45	
    46	`AlgebraicJacobian.TwoTerm.isOpen_finrank_ker_baseChange_le`
    47	(`Picard/TwoTermKernelSemicontinuity.lean`) proves openness of
    48	`{t | dim ker (k ⊗ κ(t)) ≤ e}` for `k : K → Aⁿ` with `K` finitely presented
    49	projective.  This file's theorem rewrites `p.fiberH0 M t` as exactly such a
    50	kernel dimension.  Composing them needs two things that are **still open** and
    51	are not supplied here:
    52	
    53	* the Čech difference map `𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase p M` must be *replaced* by
    54	  one of the engine's shape (`K` projective, target `Aⁿ` free).
    55	  `exists_twoTermFiniteReplacement` (`Picard/TwoTermFiniteFree.lean`:545)
    56	  produces that shape from noetherian + flat terms + f.g. cohomology, but its
    57	  `h0_bijective` field compares the replacement's `H⁰` with the original's over
    58	  every algebra, and *that* comparison — not `hbc` — is the remaining
    59	  cohomology-and-base-change content;
    60	* a **carrier transport**: the engine quantifies over `t : PrimeSpectrum A` for
    61	  a bare ring `A`, this theorem over `t : PrimeSpectrum R` with coefficient ring
    62	  `Γ(Spec R, ⊤)`.  `Scheme.ΓSpecIso R` is an isomorphism, not an equality, so
    63	  the transport is real work of the kind steps 2 and 6 perform by hand — the
    64	  obligation (c) already on record.
    65	
    66	Neither is discharged below.  What is discharged is that `hbc` is not part of
    67	either.
    68	
    69	## The junk-value caveat, which this file DOES inherit
    70	
    71	An earlier revision of this docstring said the theorem holds "with no hypotheses
    72	beyond the geometric ones" and listed what it does not need, without noting the
    73	cost.  A fresh-context review flagged the omission, and it is a real one.
    74	
    75	`Module.finrank` returns `0` in the infinite-dimensional case.  Here the
    76	coefficient ring is `Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤)`, which carries no
    77	`Field` — not even `Nontrivial` — instance in scope, and neither
    78	`FiniteDimensional` of the fibre sections nor `Module.Finite` of the Čech kernel
    79	is synthesisable.  So when the fibre sections are infinite-dimensional, **both
    80	sides read `0` and the identity is vacuously true**.  That is exactly the hazard
    81	`Picard/FiberH0Comparison.lean`:40-55 records for its own theorem, and dropping
    82	`hfin` re-opens it here for the same reason.
    83	
    84	This is *not* the same situation as
    85	`Picard/TwoTermKernelSemicontinuity.lean`, which legitimately closes the hazard:
    86	there the complex's shape (`K` finite, target `Aⁿ`) makes both fibres
    87	finite-dimensional by synthesis.  The two files were audited to different
    88	standards, and this paragraph is the correction.
    89	
    90	So the honest reading: the identity is **true unconditionally and informative
    91	where the fibre `h⁰` is finite** — which is the case of interest, since a curve's
    92	`h⁰` is finite — but the statement does not certify that finiteness itself.  A
    93	consumer wanting a non-vacuous reading must supply it, and doing so is *not* the
    94	same as supplying `hbc`; that remains the point of the restatement.
    95	
    96	## References
    97	
    98	Stacks 02KG (cohomology and base change at `i = 0`), 00NX; Mumford, *Abelian
    99	Varieties*, II §5; Hartshorne III 12.8.
   100	-/

     9	/-!
    10	# Local constancy of two-term fibre Euler indices
    11	
    12	This file records the pure commutative-algebra index carried by a
    13	`TwoTermFiniteReplacement`.  At a prime `t` of `A`, the signed dimension
    14	
    15	`dim ker(d_t) - dim coker(d_t)`
    16	
    17	of the original base-changed map equals the virtual fibre rank
    18	
    19	`rank_t(R.K0) - R.n`
    20	
    21	of any finite replacement `R`.  The right-hand side is independent of the
    22	choice of replacement and is locally constant on `PrimeSpectrum A`.
    23	
    24	The first ingredient is only a carrier bridge:
    25	`Ideal.isLocallyConstant_fiberRank` rewrites the project's residue-field
    26	`Ideal.fiberRank` as Mathlib's `Module.rankAtStalk`, whose local constancy for
    27	finitely presented flat modules is already available.  The substantive
    28	two-term step uses both universal cohomology comparisons stored in `R`:
    29	`R.h0_bijective` transports kernels and `R.h1_bijective` transports
    30	cokernels from the finite replacement to the original complex.
    31	
    32	Everything here is affine two-term algebra.  No declaration identifies this
    33	index with `Scheme.Hom.fiberEulerIndex`, sheaf or curve cohomology, a
    34	line-bundle degree, or a function on arbitrary test schemes.  In particular,
    35	this file proves neither relative-Picard or etale descent nor a PicEt degree
    36	producer.
    37	
    38	## Main declarations
    39	
    40	* `Ideal.isLocallyConstant_fiberRank`: the residue-field/stalk-rank bridge.
    41	* `TwoTermFiniteReplacement.fiberEulerIndex_eq_virtualRank`: the original
    42	  complex's signed fibre index equals the replacement's virtual rank.
    43	* `TwoTermFiniteReplacement.fiberVirtualRank_independent`: independence from
    44	  the chosen finite replacement.
    45	* `TwoTermFiniteReplacement.isLocallyConstant_fiberEulerIndex`: local
    46	  constancy of the original complex's signed fibre index on `Spec A`.
    47	-/
    48	
    49	set_option autoImplicit false
    50	
    51	universe u
    52	
    53	open Module TensorProduct
    54	
    55	namespace Ideal
    56	
    57	variable {A K : Type u} [CommRing A] [AddCommGroup K] [Module A K]
    58	
    59	/-- The residue-field fibre rank of a finitely presented flat module is
    60	locally constant on `PrimeSpectrum A`.
    61	
    62	This is a direct transport of Mathlib's
    63	`Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk` through
    64	`Ideal.finrank_fiber_eq_rankAtStalk`; it is a notation/carrier bridge rather
    65	than a new semicontinuity theorem. -/
    66	theorem isLocallyConstant_fiberRank
    67	    [Module.FinitePresentation A K] [Module.Flat A K] :
    68	    IsLocallyConstant (fun t : PrimeSpectrum A => t.asIdeal.fiberRank K) := by
    69	  convert Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk (R := A) (M := K) using 1
    70	  funext t
    71	  exact Ideal.finrank_fiber_eq_rankAtStalk t.asIdeal
    72	
    73	end Ideal
    74	
    75	namespace AlgebraicJacobian
    76	namespace TwoTermFiniteReplacement
    77	
    78	/-- The signed kernel/cokernel index of the original two-term complex after
    79	base change to `kappa(t)` equals the virtual fibre rank of any finite
    80	replacement.
    81	
    82	All subtraction is in `Int`.  This result is stronger than rearranging
    83	`TwoTerm.finrank_ker_baseChange_add_eq`: `R.h0_bijective` and
    84	`R.h1_bijective` first identify the replacement kernel and cokernel with
    85	those of the original map `d.baseChange kappa(t)`, and
    86	`TwoTerm.fiberRank_quotRange_eq_finrank_quot_baseChange` identifies the
    87	replacement cokernel rank. -/
    88	theorem fiberEulerIndex_eq_virtualRank
    89	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    90	    {M0 M1 : Type u} [AddCommGroup M0] [Module A M0]
    91	    [AddCommGroup M1] [Module A M1] {d : M0 →ₗ[A] M1}
    92	    (R : TwoTermFiniteReplacement d) (t : PrimeSpectrum A) :
    93	    (Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
    94	        (LinearMap.ker (d.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) : ℤ) -
    95	      (Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
    96	        ((t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M1) ⧸
    97	          LinearMap.range (d.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) : ℤ) =
    98	      (t.asIdeal.fiberRank R.K0 : ℤ) - (R.n : ℤ) := by
    99	  have h0 :
   100	      Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
   101	          (LinearMap.ker (R.k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) =
   102	        Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
   103	          (LinearMap.ker (d.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   104	    LinearEquiv.finrank_eq
   105	      (LinearEquiv.ofBijective
   106	        (TwoTerm.h0Map (R.k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   107	          (d.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   108	          (R.a0.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   109	          (R.a1.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   110	          (TwoTerm.baseChange_square R.k d R.a0 R.a1 t.asIdeal.ResidueField R.comm))
   111	        (R.h0_bijective t.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   112	  have h1 :
   113	      Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
   114	          ((t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] (Fin R.n → A)) ⧸
   115	            LinearMap.range (R.k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) =
   116	        Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
   117	          ((t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M1) ⧸
   118	            LinearMap.range (d.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   119	    LinearEquiv.finrank_eq
   120	      (LinearEquiv.ofBijective
   121	        (TwoTerm.h1Map (R.k.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   122	          (d.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   123	          (R.a0.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   124	          (R.a1.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   125	          (TwoTerm.baseChange_square R.k d R.a0 R.a1 t.asIdeal.ResidueField R.comm))
   126	        (R.h1_bijective t.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   127	  have hcoker :=
   128	    TwoTerm.fiberRank_quotRange_eq_finrank_quot_baseChange R.k t
   129	  have hrank := TwoTerm.finrank_ker_baseChange_add_eq R.n R.k t
   130	  omega
   131	
   132	/-- The virtual fibre rank `(rank_t R.K0 : Int) - R.n` is independent of the
   133	chosen finite replacement of the same original map.  Both sides equal the
   134	signed kernel/cokernel index of that original map. -/
   135	theorem fiberVirtualRank_independent
   136	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
   137	    {M0 M1 : Type u} [AddCommGroup M0] [Module A M0]
   138	    [AddCommGroup M1] [Module A M1] {d : M0 →ₗ[A] M1}
   139	    (R R' : TwoTermFiniteReplacement d) (t : PrimeSpectrum A) :
   140	    (t.asIdeal.fiberRank R.K0 : ℤ) - (R.n : ℤ) =
   141	      (t.asIdeal.fiberRank R'.K0 : ℤ) - (R'.n : ℤ) := by
   142	  rw [← R.fiberEulerIndex_eq_virtualRank t,
   143	    ← R'.fiberEulerIndex_eq_virtualRank t]
   144	
   145	/-- The signed kernel/cokernel index of the original base-changed two-term
   146	complex is locally constant on `PrimeSpectrum A`.
   147	
   148	The finite-projective module `R.K0` is finitely presented and flat, so its
   149	fibre rank is locally constant.  Postcomposing by `r |-> (r : Int) - R.n`
   150	and using `fiberEulerIndex_eq_virtualRank` gives the stated function.  This is
   151	only an affine module-theoretic result, with no sheaf-cohomology comparison. -/
   152	theorem isLocallyConstant_fiberEulerIndex
   153	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
   154	    {M0 M1 : Type u} [AddCommGroup M0] [Module A M0]
   155	    [AddCommGroup M1] [Module A M1] {d : M0 →ₗ[A] M1}
   156	    (R : TwoTermFiniteReplacement d) :
   157	    IsLocallyConstant (fun t : PrimeSpectrum A =>
   158	      (Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
   159	          (LinearMap.ker (d.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) : ℤ) -
   160	        (Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
   161	          ((t.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] M1) ⧸
   162	            LinearMap.range (d.baseChange t.asIdeal.ResidueField)) : ℤ)) := by
   163	  letI : Module.Flat A R.K0 := Module.Flat.of_projective
   164	  letI : Module.FinitePresentation A R.K0 :=
   165	    Module.finitePresentation_of_projective A R.K0
   166	  have h : IsLocallyConstant (fun t : PrimeSpectrum A =>
   167	      (t.asIdeal.fiberRank R.K0 : ℤ) - (R.n : ℤ)) := by
   168	    change IsLocallyConstant
   169	      ((fun r : ℕ => (r : ℤ) - (R.n : ℤ)) ∘
   170	        (fun t : PrimeSpectrum A => t.asIdeal.fiberRank R.K0))
   171	    exact (Ideal.isLocallyConstant_fiberRank (A := A) (K := R.K0)).comp
   172	      fun r => (r : ℤ) - (R.n : ℤ)
   173	  convert h using 1
   174	  funext t
   175	  exact R.fiberEulerIndex_eq_virtualRank t
   176	
   177	end TwoTermFiniteReplacement
   178	end AlgebraicJacobian

   439	/-- **Coherent-sheaf flatness of an invertible module over an affine base
   440	along a flat family.**  For a flat morphism `q : Y ⟶ T` with affine target
   441	and a locally trivial (invertible) `L` on `Y`, the module `L` is flat over
   442	`T` in the sense of `CoherentSheafFlat`: on a trivialising affine chart `W`

   444	(`isInvertible_of_restrict_iso`), which is flat over `Γ(T, ⊤)` since `q` is
   445	a flat morphism (`Flat.flat_appLE` + `Module.Flat.trans`); chart flatness
   446	globalises to every affine pair by the affine-locality engine
   447	`flat_section_of_affine_cover`. -/
   448	theorem coherentSheafFlat_of_isLocallyTrivial_of_flat {T Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T]
   449	    (q : Y ⟶ T) [AlgebraicGeometry.Flat q] {L : Y.Modules}
   450	    (hL : Scheme.LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L) :
   451	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat q L := by
   452	  haveI := hL.isFinitePresentation
   453	  choose W hxW hWaff hWtriv using hL
   454	  have heW : ∀ y : Y, W y ≤ q ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : T.Opens) := by
   455	    intro y
   456	    rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_top]
   457	    exact le_top
   458	  intro U hU V hV e
   459	  refine flat_section_of_affine_cover q L W hWaff (fun _ => (⊤ : T.Opens))
   460	    (fun _ => isAffineOpen_top T) heW (fun y => ⟨y, hxW y⟩) ?_ hU hV e
   461	  intro y
   462	  letI : Module Γ(T, ⊤) Γ(L, W y) :=
   463	    Module.compHom _ (q.appLE ⊤ (W y) (heW y)).hom
   464	  letI : Algebra Γ(T, ⊤) Γ(Y, W y) := (q.appLE ⊤ (W y) (heW y)).hom.toAlgebra
   465	  haveI hflat1 : Module.Flat Γ(T, ⊤) Γ(Y, W y) :=
   466	    q.flat_appLE (isAffineOpen_top T) (hWaff y) (heW y)
   467	  haveI : Module.Invertible Γ(Y, W y) Γ(L, W y) :=
   468	    Scheme.LineBundle.isInvertible_of_restrict_iso (W y) (hWtriv y).some
   469	  haveI : IsScalarTower Γ(T, ⊤) Γ(Y, W y) Γ(L, W y) :=
   470	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ => rfl
   471	  exact Module.Flat.trans Γ(T, ⊤) Γ(Y, W y) Γ(L, W y)

   474	an affine `π : X ⟶ Y` over `p : Y ⟶ T`, flatness of `F` over `T` (via the
   475	composite `π ≫ p`) gives flatness of `π_* F` over `T` (via `p`): the
   476	sections of `π_* F` over an affine `V` are `Γ(F, π⁻¹ V)` definitionally
   477	(with `π⁻¹ V` affine since `π` is), and the two `Γ(T, U)`-module structures
   478	agree because `(π ≫ p).appLE = p.appLE ≫ π.appLE`
   479	(`Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE`). -/
   480	theorem CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom {X Y T : Scheme.{u}}
   481	    (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom π] (p : Y ⟶ T) (F : X.Modules)
   482	    (h : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (π ≫ p) F) :
   483	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat p ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward π).obj F) := by
   484	  intro U hU V hV e
   485	  have hpre : IsAffineOpen (π ⁻¹ᵁ V) := hV.preimage π
   486	  have epre : π ⁻¹ᵁ V ≤ (π ≫ p) ⁻¹ᵁ U := by
   487	    rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage]
   488	    intro x hx
   489	    exact e hx
   490	  have base := h hU hpre epre
   491	  -- identify the two ring homomorphisms `Γ(T, U) → Γ(X, π ⁻¹ᵁ V)`
   492	  have hφ : ((π ≫ p).appLE U (π ⁻¹ᵁ V) epre).hom =

   494	    have h1 := Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE π p U V (π ⁻¹ᵁ V) e le_rfl

   501	  -- pointwise-equal ring homomorphisms

   553	/-! ## §5. Substrate for `hH1`/`hH0` — the fibre square of the finite map
   554	and the definitional Čech bridges
   555	
   556	Item (c) of the transfer package identifies `(π_A)_* L` restricted to the
   557	fibre `ℙ¹_t` with `(π_t)_* (L_t)` and transports the Čech difference map
   558	across it.  This section lands the geometric substrate: the induced finite
   559	map `π_t : C_t ⟶ ℙ¹_t` between the scheme-theoretic fibres, its cartesian
   560	square over `π_A`, and the two *definitional* Čech bridges — the difference
   561	map of a 2-affine cover for an (affine) pushforward literally *is* the
   562	difference map of the preimage cover, and surjectivity of the difference
   563	map transports across isomorphisms of module sheaves.  On top of this
   564	substrate, `hH1`/`hH0` need the affine-morphism base-change isomorphism
   565	`(p.fiberι t)^* (π_A)_* L ≅ (π_t)_* (q.fiberι t)^* L` (Stacks 02KG for the

   567	glued form of `affinePushforwardPullbackBaseChange`), plus — for `hH1` —

   573	/-- **The Čech difference map of an affine pushforward is the difference map
   574	of the preimage cover** — definitionally: sections, intersections of
   575	preimages, and restriction maps of `f_* M` over a 2-affine cover `V` all
   576	agree with those of `M` over `V.preimage f`. -/
   577	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionDiff_pushforward {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
   578	    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f] (V : Y.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : X.Modules) :
   579	    V.moduleSectionDiff ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj M) =
   580	      (V.preimage f).moduleSectionDiff M :=
   581	  rfl

   583	/-- **Naturality of the Čech difference map** in the module: a morphism of
   584	module sheaves intertwines the difference maps of a 2-affine cover. -/
   585	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionDiff_naturality {X : Scheme.{u}}
   586	    (V : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) {G G' : X.Modules} (φ : G ⟶ G')
   587	    (a : Γ(G, V.U₁)) (b : Γ(G, V.U₂)) :
   588	    V.moduleSectionDiff G' (φ.app V.U₁ a, φ.app V.U₂ b) =
   589	      φ.app (V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂) (V.moduleSectionDiff G (a, b)) := by
   590	  have h₁ := congrArg (fun (ψ : Γ(G, V.U₁) ⟶ Γ(G', V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂)) => ψ.hom a)

   592	  have h₂ := congrArg (fun (ψ : Γ(G, V.U₂) ⟶ Γ(G', V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂)) => ψ.hom b)
   593	    (φ.mapPresheaf.naturality (homOfLE (inf_le_right : V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂ ≤ V.U₂)).op)

   595	  simp only [moduleSectionDiff_apply, map_sub]

   600	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.surjective_moduleSectionDiff_of_iso {X : Scheme.{u}}

   603	    Function.Surjective ⇑(V.moduleSectionDiff G') := by
   604	  intro c

   606	  refine ⟨(e.hom.app V.U₁ a, e.hom.app V.U₂ b), ?_⟩
   607	  rw [V.moduleSectionDiff_naturality e.hom a b, hab]
   608	  change ((e.inv ≫ e.hom).app (V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂)).hom c = c
