    10	/-!
    11	# Fibrewise truncated Euler indices for line bundles
    12	
    13	For a morphism `f : X ⟶ S`, a point `s : S`, and a sheaf of modules `M` on
    14	`X`, this file defines the degree-at-most-one Euler index of the restricted
    15	module `M_s` over the residue field `kappa(s)`.  For a line bundle `L` on a
    16	relative product, it also defines the signed difference
    17	
    18	`chi(L_t) - chi(O_{(C x_S T)_t})`.
    19	
    20	The definitions deliberately use the name *index*, not geometric degree.
    21	`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.chi` is totalized: without finite-dimensional `H0` and
    22	`H1`, `Module.finrank` can read an infinite-dimensional space as zero.  The
    23	line-bundle difference becomes the usual fibre degree only after the relevant
    24	cohomological finiteness and Riemann--Roch comparison are supplied.
    25	
    26	This file proves invariance under isomorphism of the underlying modules by
    27	using `Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModulesFunctor` and the existing
    28	`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.chi_congr`.  It does not yet descend the difference
    29	through the relative Picard or etale equivalence relation, prove pullback
    30	naturality in the test scheme, or prove local constancy on that test scheme.
    31	
    32	## Main declarations
    33	
    34	* `Scheme.Hom.fiberEulerIndex`: the totalized truncated Euler index of a module
    35	  on a scheme-theoretic fibre.
    36	* `Scheme.Hom.fiberEulerIndex_eq_cech`: computation of that index by any
    37	  two-affine cover of a quasicoherent fibre module.
    38	* `Scheme.LineBundle.OnProduct.fiberEulerIndexDifference`: the signed
    39	  line-bundle index relative to the literal structure sheaf of the fibre.
    40	-/
    41	
    42	set_option autoImplicit false
    43	
    44	universe u
    45	
    46	open CategoryTheory Limits
    47	
    48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
    49	
    50	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    51	
    52	/-- The totalized degree-at-most-one Euler index of the restriction of `M` to
    53	the scheme-theoretic fibre of `f` at `s`, computed over `s`'s residue field.
    54	
    55	No properness, dimension, or cohomological finiteness hypothesis is imposed,
    56	so this is not asserted to be the genuine Euler characteristic. -/
    57	noncomputable def Hom.fiberEulerIndex (f : X ⟶ S) (s : S)
    58	    (M : X.Modules) : ℤ :=
    59	  CategoryTheory.Sheaf.chi
    60	    (toModuleKSheafOfModules
    61	      (Over.mk (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s))
    62	      (f.fiberModule s M))
    63	
    64	/-- A two-affine cover of the fibre computes `fiberEulerIndex` for a
    65	quasicoherent module.  This is an equality with the concrete signed
    66	kernel/quotient-by-range index; it does not assert finite-dimensionality. -/
    67	theorem Hom.fiberEulerIndex_eq_cech (f : X ⟶ S) (s : S)
    68	    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent]
    69	    (V : (f.fiber s).AffineCoverMVSquare) :
    70	    f.fiberEulerIndex s M =
    71	      V.chi (Over.mk (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s)) (f.fiberModule s M) := by
    72	  haveI : (f.fiberModule s M).IsQuasicoherent := f.fiberModule_isQuasicoherent s M
    73	  unfold Hom.fiberEulerIndex
    74	  exact @AffineCoverMVSquare.chi_toModuleKSheafOfModules_eq _ _
    75	    (Over.mk (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s)) V (f.fiberModule s M) this
    76	
    77	/-- `fiberEulerIndex` is invariant under an isomorphism of modules on the
    78	total space.  The isomorphism is pulled back to the fibre, restricted to the
    79	residue field, and passed to `Sheaf.chi_congr`. -/
    80	theorem Hom.fiberEulerIndex_congr (f : X ⟶ S) (s : S)
    81	    {M N : X.Modules} (e : M ≅ N) :
    82	    f.fiberEulerIndex s M = f.fiberEulerIndex s N :=
    83	  chi_toModuleKSheafOfModules_congr
    84	    (Over.mk (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s))
    85	    ((Modules.pullback (f.fiberι s)).mapIso e)
    86	
    87	namespace LineBundle.OnProduct
    88	
    89	/-- The signed, normalized fibre index of a line bundle on `C x_k T`:
    90	`chi(L_t) - chi(O_{(C x_k T)_t})`.
    91

    93	definitionally different pullback of the unit module on the total space.  This
    94	is the cohomological expression that Riemann--Roch identifies with degree once
    95	finiteness and the curve comparison are available.  At this stage it is only
    96	a totalized truncated index and has not descended to the relative Picard
    97	functor. -/

   102	  let q := pullback.snd piC piT
   103	  q.fiberEulerIndex t L.carrier -
   104	    CategoryTheory.Sheaf.chi
   105	      (toModuleKSheafOfModules
   106	        (Over.mk (q.fiberToSpecResidueField t))
   107	        (SheafOfModules.unit (q.fiber t).ringCatSheaf))

   110	underlying line-bundle modules.  This is the iso-invariance needed before a
   111	later descent to line-bundle isomorphism classes; it does not prove invariance
   112	under tensoring by a bundle pulled back from `T`. -/

   114	    {C T : Scheme.{u}} (piC : C ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
   115	    (piT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
   116	    {L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct piC piT}
   117	    (e : L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier) (t : T) :
   118	    fiberEulerIndexDifference piC piT L t =
   119	      fiberEulerIndexDifference piC piT L' t := by
   120	  dsimp [fiberEulerIndexDifference]
   121	  rw [Hom.fiberEulerIndex_congr _ _ e]
   122

    14	`Scheme.HasRigidPushforward` — `Scheme.RigidPushforwardBaseChange` — to the single module-level
    15	statement `Adelic.RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange`: bijectivity of the canonical
    16	`Γ(Spec A', ⊤) ⊗_{Γ(Spec A, ⊤)} Γ(C_A, L) → Γ(C_{A'}, g'^* L)`.  This file proves that

    19	## §1, the general theorem
    20	
    21	`exists_gammaBaseChange_of_kerPure` takes a cartesian square
    22	
    23	```
    24	  X' --g'--> X
    25	  |f'        |f
    26	  v          v
    27	  Y' --g---> Y
    28	```
    29	
    30	with `Y`, `Y'` affine and `g'` affine, a bundled 2-affine cover `𝒰` of `X`, a quasi-coherent `M`,
    31	and the Čech `H⁰`-purity hypothesis `hker` (the kernel base-change map of the two-term Čech
    32	difference `d = 𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase f M` is bijective for every `Γ(Y, ⊤)`-algebra `B`), and
    33	produces the canonical comparison
    34	
    35	`Γ(Y', ⊤) ⊗_{Γ(Y, ⊤)} Γ(f_* M, ⊤) ≅ Γ(f'_* (g'^* M), ⊤)`, `b ⊗ x ↦ b · baseMap x`.
    36	
    37	It is a sandwich of three existing pieces: the sheaf condition on both sides
    38	(`AffineCoverMVSquare.globalSectionsEquivKerModuleSectionDiffBase`, which identifies `Γ` with
    39	`ker d`), the affine-base-change Čech square on kernels
    40	(`Adelic.exists_kerChartTensorEquiv`, `Picard/RigidPushforwardChartBaseChange.lean`), and the
    41	`pushforward`-versus-`baseSections` dictionary at the two tops
    42	(`Scheme.Modules.pushforwardTopEquivBaseSections`).  The only computation is that the resulting
    43	map does send `b ⊗ x` to `b · baseMap x`, which is the restriction naturality
    44	`pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_res'` on each of the two charts.
    45	
    46	Note what is *not* assumed: `f` is arbitrary — in the application it is the proper, emphatically
    47	non-affine family `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A`, which is exactly the case
    48	`Picard/RigidPushforwardFrontier.lean` reports as having no infrastructure.
    49	
    50	Sources: Stacks 01HQ, 02KG at `i = 0`; Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, II §5; EGA III 7.7.5.
